requirement-bundles.description: A reusable baseline for defining the capability, geography, role, availability, and evidence expected from a potential responder.
Common capability, licensing, insurance, experience, and geographic requirements for work performed under professional, contractor, or trade authority.
A baseline combination for construction and trade work covering capability, license, safety, insurance or bonding, project experience, capacity, and schedule.
A qualifications-oriented combination for professional and technical services emphasizing capability, license where applicable, key personnel, experience, capacity, and approach.
A product and supplier combination covering production or supply capability, specification compliance, quality evidence, quantity capacity, lead time, and commercial terms.
An operating-condition combination for services requiring emergency availability, defined mobilization, service geography, operating hours, and delivery capacity.
A focused combination for defining a complementary delivery role, capability gap, geography, capacity, experience, and commercial assumptions for a team or supplier relationship.
A structured location-project baseline covering site control, developable area, building area, zoning, utilities, transportation access, permitting, source dates, and evidence.

governance-profiles.definition: A lighter private commercial process in which the participating organizations define the request, response, and selection practices.
governance-profiles.legal_authority_boundary: The participating organizations retain responsibility for commercial terms, diligence, legal agreements, and the authority to form any resulting relationship.

governance-profiles.definition: A private competitive process using defined requirements, response architecture, decision criteria, controlled changes, and a recorded selection.
governance-profiles.legal_authority_boundary: The RFxchange organizes the transaction record; the issuer remains responsible for commercial authority, applicable law, evaluation judgment, and contract formation.

governance-profiles.definition: A workflow for supplier discovery, teaming, readiness, or response preparation connected to a federal opportunity whose authoritative submission and award remain external.
governance-profiles.legal_authority_boundary: The RFxchange must not represent that a federal response was formally submitted or awarded when the authoritative federal system or contracting authority controls that action.

governance-profiles.definition: A governed public procurement process whose solicitation, communications, evaluation, disclosure, and award practices must conform to the applicable jurisdiction and issuer rules.
governance-profiles.legal_authority_boundary: The public issuer and its authorized procurement system retain legal authority. The RFxchange applies only the workflow explicitly approved by that issuer and must not invent governing procurement rules.

governance-profiles.definition: A structured purchasing process for an institution, anchor organization, university, health system, utility, nonprofit, or other organizational buyer.
governance-profiles.legal_authority_boundary: The institution retains its internal approvals, purchasing authority, records obligations, and contract formation responsibilities.

governance-profiles.definition: A workspace for discovery, teaming, compliance planning, drafting, and readiness when the authoritative submission, evaluation, or award occurs in another system.
governance-profiles.legal_authority_boundary: The RFxchange may record preparation activity and an external link or status, but it must not claim authoritative submission, receipt, evaluation, or award.

governance-profiles.definition: A permissioned location project using coded identities, invited responders, controlled data access, multi-organization contributions, and staged geographic decisions.
governance-profiles.legal_authority_boundary: The project representative retains authority over confidentiality, candidate participation, site visits, negotiations, incentives, and the final location decision.

readiness-rules.message_template: Describe the need or desired outcome before publication.
readiness-rules.rationale: A market request cannot be interpreted or structured without a defined need.

readiness-rules.message_template: Select the RFx request family that governs the request structure and endpoint.
readiness-rules.rationale: RFI, RFQ, RFP, qualification, supplier, teaming, and site-selection requests require different response and decision behavior.

readiness-rules.message_template: Establish the organization and authorized user responsible for issuing this request.
readiness-rules.rationale: Only an authorized organization should publish a request or represent an issuer decision.

readiness-rules.message_template: Select the governance profile and authoritative submission boundary.
readiness-rules.rationale: The platform must know whether the transaction is private, public, institutional, external-system, or confidential site-selection activity.

readiness-rules.message_template: Define the delivery, performance, service, or project geography.
readiness-rules.rationale: Geography affects discovery, matching, service territory, and responder interpretation.

readiness-rules.message_template: Set a response deadline later than publication and any required preceding events.
readiness-rules.rationale: Responders need a valid and unambiguous submission window.

readiness-rules.message_template: Move the question deadline before the response deadline.
readiness-rules.rationale: Questions and resulting controlled changes must be resolved before final submission.

readiness-rules.message_template: Add at least one structured capability, qualification, specification, commercial, or site requirement.
readiness-rules.rationale: Structured requirements drive matching, response planning, readiness, and evaluation.

readiness-rules.preferred_label: Capability terms are canonical or explicitly provisional
readiness-rules.message_template: Map each mandatory capability to an active AMACS capability or resolve its provisional status.
readiness-rules.rationale: Unreviewed free text cannot independently satisfy a hard matching gate.

readiness-rules.message_template: Select a controlled AMACS unit for each numeric, currency, duration, distance, area, or capacity qualifier.
readiness-rules.rationale: A numeric value without a unit cannot be compared reliably.

readiness-rules.preferred_label: Mandatory requirement has a decision treatment
readiness-rules.message_template: Choose whether each mandatory requirement is a gate, scored factor, gate plus scored depth, or informational item.
readiness-rules.rationale: Requirements must remain connected to the decision architecture.

readiness-rules.message_template: Confirm whether each capability requirement may be satisfied by an accepted teammate.
readiness-rules.rationale: Explicit team coverage prevents an unstated assumption from changing eligibility or match explanations.

readiness-rules.message_template: Select a response architecture template or approved custom architecture.
readiness-rules.rationale: Responders need an ordered, complete statement of what information must be supplied.

readiness-rules.message_template: Complete the instructions for every required response section.
readiness-rules.rationale: A section title alone may not tell a responder what evidence, format, or limits apply.

readiness-rules.message_template: Define whether each section may be assigned to the lead, an internal contributor, or an accepted teammate.
readiness-rules.rationale: Ownership rules support collaborative response planning without implying that a platform invitation forms a legal agreement.

readiness-rules.message_template: Select a decision architecture or approved custom decision process.
readiness-rules.rationale: The issuer should establish the decision method before publication.

readiness-rules.message_template: Adjust weighted decision factors so the total equals 100 percent.
readiness-rules.rationale: A weighted model is not interpretable when its disclosed factor weights do not reconcile.

readiness-rules.preferred_label: Decision factor has an evidence source
readiness-rules.message_template: Link every comparative decision factor to at least one requirement, response section, or structured data field.
readiness-rules.rationale: Evaluators need a disclosed source of evidence for each factor.

readiness-rules.preferred_label: Scored capability requirements use capability fit
readiness-rules.message_template: Add or link the Capability fit and depth factor for capability requirements scored beyond minimum coverage.
readiness-rules.rationale: A capability requirement marked for comparative scoring must be represented in the decision architecture.

readiness-rules.preferred_label: Gate and score do not duplicate the same fact
readiness-rules.message_template: Review criteria that appear to award points for the same fact already used as a pass/fail gate.
readiness-rules.rationale: Minimum compliance and comparative depth may both be used, but the identical fact should not be counted twice.

readiness-rules.preferred_label: Requested price has a disclosed treatment
readiness-rules.message_template: Add a price or cost factor, or explicitly mark requested pricing as informational.
readiness-rules.rationale: Requesting price without explaining its decision treatment creates ambiguity for responders and evaluators.

readiness-rules.message_template: Link each required response section to a requirement, readiness obligation, or decision factor.
readiness-rules.rationale: The platform should not burden responders with required material that has no identified use.

readiness-rules.message_template: Resolve missing, inaccessible, quarantined, or unauthorized attachments.
readiness-rules.rationale: A published RFx must not depend on material that responders cannot access.

readiness-rules.message_template: State whether submission occurs in The RFxchange or an authoritative external system.
readiness-rules.rationale: The platform must never falsely represent completion of an external formal submission.

readiness-rules.preferred_label: Information-only request has a non-award endpoint
readiness-rules.message_template: Replace the award endpoint with information review, source identification, shortlist, connection, or another appropriate conclusion.
readiness-rules.rationale: An RFI, Sources Sought, qualifications request, teaming request, or site-selection RFI does not automatically end in a procurement award.

readiness-rules.message_template: Configure coded identity, invited participation, and access controls for the location project.
readiness-rules.rationale: Site-selection projects commonly require controlled project and candidate information throughout staged evaluation.

readiness-rules.preferred_label: Site data include units and source dates
readiness-rules.message_template: Add the controlled unit and source date for each quantitative site, utility, workforce, infrastructure, and cost value.
readiness-rules.rationale: Location comparisons require comparable units and time-specific data provenance.

readiness-rules.message_template: Confirm the authority and assigned sections of each EDO, locality, utility, property, workforce, or other project contributor.
readiness-rules.rationale: A multi-party community response needs explicit ownership and access boundaries.

readiness-rules.message_template: Display the authoritative external submission destination and platform limitation notice.
readiness-rules.rationale: Users must understand that preparation activity in The RFxchange is not authoritative submission or receipt.

readiness-rules.message_template: Resolve every blocking publication-readiness finding before publishing.
readiness-rules.rationale: Publication is the controlled transition that activates matching, notifications, response timelines, and the auditable RFx lifecycle.

Obtain bids against defined specifications under an applicable competitive process.

Identify organizations with complementary capabilities for a potential joint response or business relationship.
Request an ordinary commercial product, service, referral recipient, or provider through a lighter structured process.

request-families.purpose: Compare communities, sites, buildings, workforce, infrastructure, costs, and implementation conditions for a location decision.

market-roles.definition: Creates, fabricates, assembles, grows, extracts, or otherwise produces a physical or digital product supplied into a market.
Transforms raw, intermediate, or recovered inputs into a processed, refined, formulated, or otherwise marketable output.
Performs an intangible, professional, technical, operational, institutional, or community service for another party or beneficiary.
Operates an ongoing facility, system, business process, network, venue, fleet, program, or other productive activity as a continuing market function.
Sells goods or services primarily to end users or consumers through physical, digital, direct, or omnichannel channels.
Aggregates, warehouses, markets, or distributes goods or supplies between producers and downstream commercial, institutional, or retail buyers.
Moves people, freight, commodities, energy, information, or other transferable value through a managed transportation or transmission service.
Operates a digital or physical platform that enables discovery, interaction, exchange, transactions, distribution, or participation among multiple market sides.
Operates infrastructure or a network whose availability, capacity, or connectivity enables other market participants to function.
Assumes, prices, pools, transfers, or administers specified financial or insurable risks in exchange for premium, consideration, or contractual terms.
Provides credit, financing, lending capacity, or credit-bearing facilities to individuals, organizations, transactions, or assets.
Facilitates payments, securities, deposits, capital formation, custody, brokerage, clearing, or other financial transactions between market participants.
Manages investment portfolios, pooled assets, fiduciary capital, or other financial assets under a defined mandate for owners or beneficiaries.
Owns or controls a productive, financial, real, intellectual, or infrastructure asset whose use, lease, development, or deployment participates in the market.
Creates, develops, constructs, improves, or brings a site, facility, product, project, or asset from concept toward operational or market-ready condition.
Creates, curates, publishes, broadcasts, streams, or distributes informational, entertainment, advertising, or other media content as a market activity.
Authorizes another party to use intellectual property, a brand, a business system, a controlled right, or other licensed market asset under defined terms.
Creates, sponsors, funds, purchases, commissions, or issues a market need, request, acquisition, investment, program, or other demand-side opportunity.

outcome-types.definition: Whether the committed product, service, work, transaction, or other market activity reached its required completion or acceptance state.
The degree to which delivery, response, milestone, availability, or other performance occurred within the required or expected time window.
The degree to which delivered work, products, services, or results met defined quality, specification, defect, accuracy, or conformance expectations.
The degree to which the activity achieved the intended functional, operational, programmatic, mission, or beneficiary result.
The realized cost, savings, revenue, return, price performance, economic value, or other financial effect associated with the activity or decision.
The extent to which an intended user, customer, participant, organization, or market adopted, consumed, used, or sustained the delivered capability or result.
The observed satisfaction, experience, confidence, trust, accessibility, or other stakeholder-perceived effect associated with delivery or use.
The realized safety, incident, loss, exposure, resilience, security, or other risk-related result associated with the activity or decision.
Whether the delivered activity or result satisfied applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, policy, credential, audit, or standards obligations.
The realized environmental, resource-efficiency, emissions, waste, circularity, conservation, or other sustainability effect associated with delivery or use.
The realized ability of an organization, system, network, facility, workforce, or supply chain to sustain, absorb, scale, recover, or continue required performance.
The realized learning, process improvement, capability enhancement, innovation, or other positive change generated through the activity and suitable for future market learning.
